status: Seat arrangement from the Polish Osa-AK manual's cabin plan (mon_2112_80 Fig. 3, pp. 23–25), confirmed by WZU camera views of a Polish crew at work (grezicki_wzu Fig. 4): driver front left, commander front right, the three operators on one bench along the left wall facing the main console SŁ-2M, front to rear guidance (deputy commander), search (senior operator), range (operator). The operator panels are SAM Simulator's photographs of the three columns (samsim_panels), at 1 mm per pixel: every control, lamp and screen sits where it is in those photos, cross-checked against real-cabin photos (cabin_photos) and the game's sprite positions. Distances between seats, the columns' height above the floor and the controls the game has no picture for are SAM3D estimates that only need to be reachable and readable. Lamp meanings follow the SAM Simulator manual where it gives them.
notes: Body frame: metres, x right, y forward, z up, from the ground under the hull centre. The placeholder hull in Unreal is 9.1 x 2.8 m with its roof at 2.2 m. Lamp sources use the source ids of data/procedures/osa_ak.json. Red dots (red_dot) are only given where a picture shows one: they mark a control's working position, not where it starts (docs/research/OSA_CONSOLE_MAP_2026-10.md §12).

displays.source: docs/research/OSA_MANUALS_2026-10.md (the strip: ΔД, Δε, β and ε of the tracking radar); cabin_photos (opisybroni 54539); cabin_photos (user_modernised_2 (eight counters); captions under them include ΔД, Δε, АЗИМУТ ССЦ, УГОЛ МЕСТА ССЦ, СВР I, II)
displays.notes: Left to right: ΔД (metres between the range gate and the echo in it), Δε (mils between the antenna's elevation and the echo's), the SSC azimuth rough then fine counter, the SSC elevation rough then fine counter, and the two СВР (missile channel) places, not read yet. Angles are in mils (6000 to the circle, XX-YY; samsim_osa p16): rough = the hundreds, fine = the rest. Which counter reads what, and what exactly the deviations are, is our reading of the manual's one-line description and the photographs.

displays.label: TOV monitor
displays.notes: The camera looks along the SSC azimuth and elevation with the wide or narrow lens; crosshair at the centre.

displays.label: εс
displays.notes: SSC elevation in Russian military angle (15-00 = 90 deg); ПОДСВЕТКА lights it. Dial face: SAM3D estimate.

displays.label: ДЦ
displays.notes: Measured target distance, 10 V = 10 km. Reads while the SSC tracks in range (the range wheel follows the target then); rests at 0 otherwise. Full scale 30 V: SAM3D estimate.

displays.label: ЗК-4 (Qc)
displays.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p48 (the course setter ЗК-4 has a scale the heading is set on)
displays.notes: Dial face in degrees: SAM3D estimate.

displays.label: OR-31M Qc scale
displays.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p48 (agreement is checked on the Qc scale of block OR-31M, which stops turning once the course setter's and the GA-3's selsyns agree), p52 (OR-31M carries the follow-up systems' scales)
displays.notes: Shows the gyro half-compass's heading, so it turns while the gyro is slaved to the setter and stops when they agree. Dial face in mils (60-00 to the circle) and its place on the block: SAM3D estimates.

displays.label: ШИРОТА
displays.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p51-52 (potentiometer φ with the scale ШИРОТА on block 0005-8M)
displays.notes: Degrees of latitude, 0-90 over three quarters of a turn: SAM3D estimate of the face.

displays.label: Elevation-search indicator OS81-10M
displays.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p95 (two-coordinate sector indicator, rectangular raster, brightness mark; 31° of elevation and 2 km of range centred on the tracking radar's range gate; three ranges for search beams I, II, III; the antenna scans in elevation within the beam during ЦУ), Fig. 2.37 p97 (beam I −1° to 5°, II 3° to 9°, III 6° to 30°); samsim_panels (position: the round screen right of the TV monitor)
displays.notes: One raster per search beam of the console's elevation_search (I, II, III), placed as in Fig. 2.37 (approximate); it shows the beam the antenna searches, and the antenna's sweep and target marks come from the engagement model. Afterglow 1.5 s: SAM3D estimate.
